description: Normalised key figures extracted from six independently-designed city blueprints (claude-code-haiku, claude-code-sonnet, claude-code-opus-4.8, claude-code-fable/worldwide-city, chat-gpt-code/resilient-city and claude-code-opus). Every figure carries a status: 'stated' (explicitly in the source repo), 'derived' (arithmetic on stated figures, formula noted), or 'missing' (the source repo does not report it — value is null, never inferred).
model_label_note: The 'model' field records which model authored each design. Only the two Opus repos carry an explicit version in their repo name (claude-code-opus-4.8 and claude-code-opus, the latter being Opus 5's). The Haiku, Sonnet and Fable repos do not record a minor version anywhere in their contents, so those labels are deliberately unversioned rather than guessed.
repo_rename_note: CIVITAS's source repo was renamed from 'claude-code-opus' to 'claude-code-opus-4.8' when Opus 5's HEARTH took over the 'claude-code-opus' name. The repo field below reflects the CURRENT names.
comparability_warnings: CRIME TARGETS ARE NOT DIRECTLY COMPARABLE: Solaris targets 15 total crimes/100k/yr, Meridian-S targets <150 VIOLENT crimes/100k/yr, and CIVITAS, Meridian-F, Resilient City and HEARTH target homicide rates (<1, <0.5, <2 and <0.5 per 100k/yr respectively — Resilient City and HEARTH add separate overall-offence sub-targets). These are different metrics.

RESPONSE TIMES ARE NOT DIRECTLY COMPARABLE: definitions differ — Solaris reports simulated travel medians, Meridian-S reports travel-to-farthest-resident seconds, CIVITAS and Resilient City report end-to-end (call to on-scene) including dispatch+turnout, Meridian-F reports turnout+travel, and HEARTH reports travel and total separately at p50/p90/p99. Each figure carries a 'definition' field.

DENSITY BASIS DIFFERS: Solaris's 1,965 km2 footprint includes agricultural rings inside the city boundary; the others exclude their hinterland from the urban area. Solaris does not state a built-up-only density.

SEISMIC DESIGN BASES ARE EXPRESSED IN DIFFERENT UNITS: Solaris and Meridian-F give a MAGNITUDE (9.0 Mw, M8+/M7), HEARTH gives a RETURN PERIOD (2,475-year), and Meridian-S, CIVITAS and Resilient City give a PERFORMANCE FRAMEWORK (MCE / Immediate Occupancy) with no number at all. The simulator can only score damage against a magnitude, so the latter four fall back to a flagged generic M8.0.

MODEL VERSIONS ARE ONLY PARTLY KNOWN: the two Opus repos state their version (4.8 and 5); the Haiku, Sonnet and Fable repos record no minor version anywhere, so those labels are unversioned rather than guessed.

seismic_design_basis.note: a RETURN PERIOD, not a magnitude — no Mw figure anywhere, so the simulator falls back to a generic M8.0 MCE and flags it

base_isolation_scope.value: acute hospital, 6 district health centres, emergency operations centre, all 7 stations, water plants (lead-rubber or friction pendulum, isolated period 3.0-3.5 s)

soft_storey_ban.note: capacity design, rocking walls and non-structural restraint are specified in detail, but no explicit soft-storey prohibition appears (contrast Meridian-F/S, which ban it outright)

drift_capacity_m.note: expressed as a residual drift RATIO, not the absolute lateral displacement Solaris gives (1.5 m) — not directly comparable

quake_survival_target_pct.note: no % survival figure; the target is functional instead ('repairable, re-occupiable in 30 days'), which the repo argues is the more demanding objective

tsunami_design_height_m.unit: m engineered berm (+1.5 km coastal forest belt behind it)
tsunami_design_height_m.note: berm height is stated; the design INUNDATION height itself is not numbered — it is specified relationally as 'inundation + 3 m freeboard' (Art. 26)

flood_defence_layers.value: core founded above design inundation (terrace raised where topography fails, Rikuzentakata precedent); 12 m engineered berm carrying the structural duty; 1.5 km coastal forest for sediment/scour/amenity only (explicitly NOT trusted as barrier after 2011); 71 vertical-evacuation refuges at 500 m spacing checked for buoyancy, scour, debris impact and overturning per ASCE 7 ch.6 / FEMA P-646

site_elevation_model.value: partial — core above design inundation, coastal terrace raised (>10 m scale stated), Class F soils excluded from the urban core; no terrain map

stormwater_drainage.value: daylighted swales within the 22% green allocation, sized for the projected 2150 1-in-200-year rainfall; park network doubles as designed flood storage ('Room for the River' logic)
stormwater_drainage.note: only design of the six to state a dated future-climate rainfall design standard

wind_design.value: roofing mechanically fixed to the 1,700-year gust; aerodynamic shaping (chamfered/stepped corners); impact-rated glazing or shutters in cyclone regions; continuous load path with tension ties; PV rated to Risk Category IV uplift with trackers stowing, and a 72-hour stow carried by dispatchable backstop

fire_stations.note: 6 district + 1 civic, sited by greedy p-median over 625 candidate avenue intersections; PLUS 60 ward posts with a duty first responder on an e-bike and a pre-positioned cache

fire_response_median_min.source: stated dispatch 64 s + turnout 80 s + stated engine travel p50 65.4 s = 209.4 s
fire_response_median_min.definition: end-to-end call-to-on-scene median; the repo reports p90 (4:02) and travel percentiles rather than a total median

fire_response_p95_min.unit: min (p90 total; travel p99 2:04; full alarm assignment p90 6:19)
fire_response_p95_min.definition: end-to-end p90 (dispatch+turnout+travel) against NFPA 1710's 4:00 travel benchmark, which its travel p90 of 1:38 clears by a wide margin

ems_response_median_min.source: stated ALS total p90 222.1 s minus travel p90 98.1 s = 124 s fixed, + stated travel p50 65.4 s
ems_response_median_min.definition: ALS ambulance end-to-end median; separately, ward-responder collapse-to-defibrillation is a STATED p50 2:28 / p90 2:54

ems_ambulances.note: 7 stations and 60 e-bike ward posts are specified, but no ambulance vehicle count

police_response_target_min.note: no police response-time target; police are unarmed by default and mental-health/welfare/intoxication calls are routed to unarmed health teams instead (CAHOOTS precedent)

police_stations.note: the 7 stations are fire/EMS; police facilities are never enumerated

hospitals.value: 1 acute hospital (base-isolated) + 6 district health centres; health centre reachable by bike p90 3.4 min

response_degraded_scenario.value: 300 Monte-Carlo trials of the design earthquake with 2 of 7 stations lost and debris blockage by street class (lanes 12%, collectors 5%, avenues 2%): engine travel p90 2:16 (worst decile 2:50), mean 136 people with no vehicle route (worst trial 983), foot response from ward cache p90 5:32, unreachable even on foot 0.05%
response_degraded_scenario.note: most rigorous degraded-case analysis of the six; also runs a speed sensitivity (still clears benchmark at 60% of assumed speeds)

crime_target.unit: homicides per 100k/yr (plus <=1,200 recorded offences per 100k/yr, rolling decade)

economic_model.value: Plan the substrate, market the superstructure — three layers
mechanisms: Layer 1 Commons ~35% of consumption (land, water, grid, transport, digital, health, education, staple food floor, housing tenure) at cost or free
Layer 2 Market ~55% with real prices/profit/failure; worker cooperative is the default legal form with tax and procurement preference
Layer 3 Contribution ~10% (care, culture, maintenance, emergency corps) via civic dividend and non-convertible time credits
city owns all land in perpetuity, never sells; 99-year transferable mortgageable ground leases; ground rent is the primary public revenue (LVT in all but name)
8:1 total compensation ratio cap within any single firm
Job Guarantee at base wage within 14 days of application

gini_target.note: no Gini figure; an 8:1 intra-firm compensation ratio cap is stated instead, with inequality named as the strongest cross-national correlate of homicide

energy_demand_avg_mw.note: 5,250 kWh/person/yr delivered electricity, inclusive of industry, food, water, transport and steelmaking

energy_demand_peak_mw.note: no peak load stated; storage power ratings are given (700 MW battery, 260 MW charge / 145 MW discharge long-duration) but these are not a demand peak

energy_mix.value: 372 MW wind (62 x 6 MW) + 795 MWp PV (145 roof + 650 agrivoltaic over ~810 ha) + 12 MW hydro + 90 MW biomass CHP; 2,162 GWh/yr generation = x1.65 overbuild; biomass only 11.8% of demand from 417 km2 forest

battery_storage_gwh.unit: GWh battery (700 MW) + 160 GWh long-duration (~104 GWh deliverable after round-trip losses)

energy_autonomy_days.source: ~104 GWh deliverable long-duration storage / 3.60 GWh mean daily demand
energy_autonomy_days.note: the repo does NOT frame this as an autonomy figure — it instead reports a 20-year hourly simulation giving 'Lean Mode' rationing 4 h/yr mean, 28 h in the worst of 20 years, and unserved energy 0.015% of demand in that worst year

water_demand.note: 10.0 domestic (110 L/person/day) + 4.1 industrial + 9.8 irrigation; margin x7.9 mean and x4.9 in a 1-in-100 dry year

water_sources.value: 975 km2 catchment yield 190 Mm3/yr mean (118 Mm3/yr in a 1-in-100 dry year) at 750 mm rainfall and 0.26 runoff coefficient; all wastewater treated to reuse standard and returned to irrigation and industry; struvite phosphorus recovery

water_reserve_days.note: the repo frames this as carrying a three-consecutive-dry-year sequence rather than as a days figure

food_self_sufficiency.value: Tier 1 (water, calories, protein, heat, shelter, sanitation, essential medicines, electricity) achieved indefinitely from territory: 306 km2 cropland+pasture, 0.12 ha/person, 2,550 kcal/day at the plate, 16.9% of calories from animals, grossed up x1.368 for loss/waste/seed

food_reserve_months.unit: months staple food (distributed silos, not one central)
food_reserve_months.note: plus 90 days of critical spares and a 20-year Tier 3 strategic stock

housing_floor_m2_per_person.unit: m2/person city-wide provision (statutory minimum 28 m2 for a one-person home, +12 m2 per additional occupant)
housing_floor_m2_per_person.note: highest provision of the six; also mandates dual aspect, >=2 h winter-solstice sun, >=2.7 m ceilings, >=5 m2 private outdoor space

noise_limit_db.value: <=50 dB Lden at facade, <=30 dB LAeq in bedrooms at night
noise_limit_db.note: the repo flags this itself as 'at the optimistic end of the evidence' — a target with a monitoring duty, achievable only because there is no through motor traffic

commute_target.value: bicycle commute p90 8.4 min (max 11.6); health centre by bike p90 3.4 min; ward hub within a 10-min walk for 100% (p90 5.2 min); park within 300 m for 99.8%
commute_target.note: modelled on the actual network by models/amenity_access_model.py, not asserted

local_reserve_hours.unit: hours (cool refuge within 400 m holding <=30 C wet-bulb for 72 h with no grid power or fuel, Art. 27)
local_reserve_hours.note: every ward also holds an emergency cache and duty responder; trained citizen responders >=1 per 15 residents (~16,700 people)

fire.notes: Best-dimensioned fabric of the six: 100 m block lattice, 12/22/34 m street hierarchy, 12 m lanes named explicitly as fire breaks, sprinklers throughout, encapsulated mass timber with calculated charring depth, no domestic gas, and a 200 m WUI buffer. The city being timber cuts both ways and the repo says so.

flood.notes: 12 m berm height stated, 71 vertical-evacuation refuges with modelled walk times (p99.9 8:49 against a 10:00 budget), stormwater sized to a projected 2150 1-in-200-year rainfall. The design inundation depth itself is given only relationally (inundation + 3 m freeboard), so the overtopping threshold is still user-set.

quake.notes: Runs its own 300-trial degraded case with street-class debris blockage and 2 of 7 stations lost. Isolation scope and rocking-wall system are specific. Caveat: the design basis is a 2,475-year RETURN PERIOD with no magnitude, so damage is scored against a generic M8.0 (flagged), and no explicit soft-storey ban is stated.

population.notes: The most measured of the six: 40 m2/person, ward hub within a 5-min walk for 100%, park within 300 m for 99.8%, plus job guarantee, 8:1 pay cap and Commons tier — all modelled on the network rather than asserted.
